title: Simple Search
story: Ctrl+F. The most-used feature in every browser, editor, and document reader. Finding a word in text seems simple, but the algorithm behind it is elegant. Build your own search that finds every occurrence and returns the positions — then extend it to case-insensitive search.
why: Substring search teaches pattern matching, sliding window technique, and the fundamental text operation that powers everything from grep to Google.
analogy: Looking for a specific Lego brick in a long chain of bricks. You slide a window the size of the search pattern along the chain, checking if the colors match at each position. The sliding window is your search algorithm — methodically checking every possible position.
try_it: Implement `count_matches` that returns just the count. Add `replace_all` that replaces every occurrence of pattern with replacement text. Search for 'the' in a paragraph — how many false positives from 'there', 'then', 'other'? Add word-boundary checking.
tips: Slide a window of pattern.len() across text, stopping at text.len() - pattern.len()
Break early on first mismatch — no need to check remaining characters
Case-insensitive search: convert both characters to same case before comparing
common_mistakes: Going past text.len() - pattern.len() — you'll access out-of-bounds indices
Not handling empty pattern — it matches everywhere but that's usually not intended
Returning position + 1 instead of position — computer indices start at 0
